biography: Bernardo de Lima, a name synonymous with both brilliance and baffling inconsistency in the Kart 4 series, hails from the sun-drenched favelas of Rio de Janeiro. His introduction to racing was less glamorous than most; not through karting schools or wealthy benefactors, but by tearing through the winding alleys on a souped-up delivery moped, dodging stray dogs and oblivious pedestrians. One fateful delivery, he stumbled upon a local karting track, and after some persistent begging, was allowed a few laps. His raw talent was immediately apparent, even if his technique was… unconventional. De Lima quickly rose through the regional ranks, known for his aggressive overtaking and devil-may-care attitude. However, his career has been plagued by costly errors and moments of inexplicable hesitation, preventing him from reaching his full potential. Now, at 38, De Lima is considered a veteran of the Kart 4 circuit, a fan favorite whose flashes of brilliance are often overshadowed by moments of utter frustration.
drivingStyle: De Lima's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward gamble. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and fearless dives into corners, often pushing the limits of his kart and the patience of his rivals. He’s a master of the oversteer, wrestling the kart into submission rather than coaxing it. While this aggressive approach can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also frequently results in costly spins and collisions. Tire management is not his forte, as he tends to burn through rubber in his relentless pursuit of speed. Under pressure, De Lima can either rise to the occasion with a stunning drive or completely implode, revealing a startling lack of composure.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles. Silva, known for his calculated and precise driving, often criticizes De Lima's reckless abandon, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track.

A battle of generations. Costa, a young up-and-comer, sees De Lima as a fading star, while De Lima views Costa as an arrogant rookie who needs to earn her stripes, resulting in fierce on-track battles.
A longstanding feud stemming from a controversial collision in the 2018 Rio Grand Prix, where De Lima was accused of deliberately taking Rodriguez out of the race.

quirks: Always wears a faded Senna t-shirt under his race suit.
Refuses to start a race without first sprinkling a pinch of Rio beach sand on his tires.
Has a lucky charm – a small, carved wooden monkey – that he keeps hidden in his kart.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being perfect, it's about being fearless. If you're not on the edge, you're taking up too much space."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2016 Interlagos Karting Championship in front of his home crowd, a moment that brought tears to his eyes and solidified his status as a local hero.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2019 Sao Paulo Grand Prix, handing the victory to his arch-rival Ricardo Silva and facing intense criticism from the media.
